note: Hand-researched editorial content. Merged into the generated catalogue at build time; never written by the generator. Entries are re-matched by sourceFeatureId if candidate ids change. Every claim is traceable to a URL in `sources`; `sourceVerification` records whether the cited page was retrieved or only listed. `motorcycleEvidence: none-found` is a recorded research outcome, not a placeholder.

osm-mountain-pass-0294170e7982ca2f.name: Horseshoe Pass (A542)
osm-mountain-pass-0294170e7982ca2f.riderNote: The A542 between Llangollen and Llandegla, topping out at 417 m. The Ponderosa café at the summit is one of the best-known biker meeting points in north Wales.
osm-mountain-pass-0294170e7982ca2f.busyPeriods: Very busy with bikes on fine weekends, which is the appeal and also the risk - expect oncoming riders using the whole road.

osm-mountain-pass-0487edfe6a27cbd3.name: Honister Pass (B5289)
osm-mountain-pass-0487edfe6a27cbd3.riderNote: The B5289 over Honister at 356 m, joining Seatoller in Borrowdale to Gatesgarth at the foot of Buttermere, with gradients reaching 1 in 4. One of the six passes on MyRoute-app's Lake District motorcycle loop.
osm-mountain-pass-0487edfe6a27cbd3.busyPeriods: Peak holiday season is heavy between the Honister slate mine and Seatoller, and Cumberland Council has imposed emergency speed and weight restrictions here after culvert damage. Lake District leisure traffic peaks on summer weekends and school holidays.

osm-mountain-pass-0756e026f085fa16.name: Clee Hill (A4117)
osm-mountain-pass-0756e026f085fa16.riderNote: The A4117 crossing Clee Hill at 381 m between Ludlow and Cleobury Mortimer - a long drag up and over, with views across Shropshire from the top. BestBikingRoads rates it 3 out of 5 overall, 4 for both corners and scenery.
osm-mountain-pass-0756e026f085fa16.enforcementNote: BestBikingRoads reviewers score police presence 3 out of 5 on this road. OpenStreetMap records no camera or enforcement relation here.

osm-mountain-pass-0852ddb9cc7e50e1.name: Windy Gap (Slievenaboley Road)
osm-mountain-pass-0852ddb9cc7e50e1.riderNote: A viewpoint saddle on the Slievenaboley Road in the Dromara Hills, within the Mourne and Slieve Croob National Landscape, south-west of Dromara. Not the Mourne Windy Gap between Eagle Mountain and Slievemoughanmore, which has no road over it.

osm-mountain-pass-199be36cc57bff57.name: Grindleton Fell (Smalden Lane)
osm-mountain-pass-199be36cc57bff57.riderNote: A 269 m crossing on Smalden Lane above Grindleton, on the Ribble Valley side of the Forest of Bowland. Discover Bowland's hill-climb route swings back over Grindleton Fell into the Ribble Valley. OpenStreetMap maps no speed limit on this lane.

osm-mountain-pass-1a61bdf3ce3c509c.name: Whinlatter Pass (B5292)
osm-mountain-pass-1a61bdf3ce3c509c.riderNote: The B5292 between Braithwaite and Lorton, the northernmost of the Lake District passes and the only one with a forest visitor centre on it. Two lanes throughout, which makes it the gentlest of the group.
osm-mountain-pass-1a61bdf3ce3c509c.busyPeriods: Whinlatter Forest's visitor centre sits on the pass, so it carries family and visitor traffic through the day in season.

osm-mountain-pass-3065197c08081161.name: Bowland Knotts (Keasden Road)
osm-mountain-pass-3065197c08081161.riderNote: The second of the two eastern Bowland fell roads, crossing at 422 m on Keasden Road between Slaidburn and Clapham. Discover Bowland calls the climb steady and graded, with a steep and sometimes technical descent through Gisburn Forest. OpenStreetMap maps no speed limit on this way.
osm-mountain-pass-3065197c08081161.busyPeriods: Discover Bowland describes both eastern Bowland fell roads as effectively single track for much of their length across quiet moorland.

osm-mountain-pass-309fb201a2d838f8.name: Gospel Pass
osm-mountain-pass-309fb201a2d838f8.riderNote: The highest road pass in Wales at 550 m, crossing the Black Mountains between Hay-on-Wye and Llanthony. Largely single-track with grass down the middle in places and open sheep grazing.
osm-mountain-pass-309fb201a2d838f8.busyPeriods: Heavily used on summer weekends and bank holidays; the single-track sections back up badly with oncoming cars.

osm-mountain-pass-3337fe91b9e7d4af.name: Buttertubs Pass
osm-mountain-pass-3337fe91b9e7d4af.riderNote: Roughly 5.3 miles of open moorland road between Hawes and Thwaite in the Yorkshire Dales, named for the limestone potholes near the summit that resemble butter churns.
osm-mountain-pass-3337fe91b9e7d4af.busyPeriods: Popular on summer weekends; unfenced with livestock on the road.

osm-mountain-pass-35fdaa4d7b985688.name: Witchie Knowe
osm-mountain-pass-35fdaa4d7b985688.riderNote: A saddle on a single-track unclassified road in Yarrow, Scottish Borders, on the crossing between the Ettrick and Yarrow valleys. OpenStreetMap maps no elevation. No motorcycle-route source was found that names it.

osm-mountain-pass-4243a6a10085c394.name: Trough of Bowland (Trough Road)
osm-mountain-pass-4243a6a10085c394.riderNote: The single-track Trough Road through the Trough of Bowland, the classic crossing between Dunsop Bridge and the headwaters of the Wyre, with a short steep pull through Sykes. BestBikingRoads carries a 68 km route through it rated 4 out of 5.

osm-mountain-pass-4316c5bf2f66837c.name: Bwlch y Groes (Hellfire Pass)
osm-mountain-pass-4316c5bf2f66837c.riderNote: The second highest paved pass in Wales at 546 m, running from Llanymawddwy to Llanuwchllyn. Known as Hellfire Pass for the sustained steep climb; it forms part of the Welsh Super 10 route.
osm-mountain-pass-4316c5bf2f66837c.busyPeriods: Quiet by Welsh-pass standards; busiest on fine summer weekends.

osm-mountain-pass-67089b4de30ca775.name: Newlands Pass (Newlands Hause)
osm-mountain-pass-67089b4de30ca775.riderNote: Mapped at 333 m on the unclassified road between Buttermere and Braithwaite, also known as Newlands Hause. OpenStreetMap records it as roughly a lane and a half wide, and the Buttermere side carries the steepest ramps of the northern Lakes passes.
osm-mountain-pass-67089b4de30ca775.busyPeriods: Lake District leisure traffic peaks on summer weekends and school holidays. A lane-and-a-half road does not absorb it.

osm-mountain-pass-69c478fbd704733b.name: Bwlch-y-maen (B4410)
osm-mountain-pass-69c478fbd704733b.riderNote: A saddle on the B4410 above Llanfrothen in Eryri, on the Garreg-to-Maentwrog road. Rush Magazine's north Wales driving-roads guide lists the B4410 as a rollercoaster B-road that pinches to single track around Rhyd. No motorcycle-specific source names it.

osm-mountain-pass-72974bf7b019ec99.name: The Gap (Mull of Kintyre road)
osm-mountain-pass-72974bf7b019ec99.riderNote: A saddle on the single-track unclassified road at the south end of Kintyre, about a kilometre east of the Mull of Kintyre lighthouse. Frommer's describes the narrow road from Southend reaching the gap, beyond which the 2.5 km down to the lighthouse is a walk rather than a ride.

osm-mountain-pass-731b90be58af1992.name: Cairnwell Pass (A93)
osm-mountain-pass-731b90be58af1992.riderNote: At 670 m the highest main road in the UK, carrying the A93 Old Military Road between Spittal of Glenshee and Braemar past the Glenshee Ski Centre at the summit. The Devil's Elbow double hairpin sits about a mile south of the top.
osm-mountain-pass-731b90be58af1992.busyPeriods: Ski-centre traffic in winter and snowgate closures; tourist coaches on the Snow Roads route in summer.

osm-mountain-pass-7c9a1e3e4cb0b8b1.name: Swinhope Head
osm-mountain-pass-7c9a1e3e4cb0b8b1.riderNote: The summit of the single-track moor crossing between Westgate in Weardale and Newbiggin in Teesdale. OpenStreetMap records no elevation on the node and maps the way as one lane. No motorcycle-route source was found that names it.

osm-mountain-pass-80bd39d23e8e26b2.name: Clay Bank Top (B1257)
osm-mountain-pass-80bd39d23e8e26b2.riderNote: The 268 m summit of the B1257 Stokesley-to-Helmsley road, known to riders as the Yorkshire TT, dropping off the moor edge down Clay Bank past Chop Gate. BestBikingRoads rates the road 4.1 out of 5 overall and 4.6 for corners.
osm-mountain-pass-80bd39d23e8e26b2.busyPeriods: Busier at weekends. BestBikingRoads reviewers report a consistent police presence and frequent crashes on sunny summer weekends, and recommend riding it midweek.
osm-mountain-pass-80bd39d23e8e26b2.enforcementNote: BestBikingRoads reviewers describe a regular police presence on summer weekends. OpenStreetMap records no camera or enforcement relation here, which is a gap in the map rather than an absence of enforcement.

osm-mountain-pass-8afd88e9efcac81b.name: Merrybent Hill
osm-mountain-pass-8afd88e9efcac81b.riderNote: A 321 m saddle on an unnamed single-carriageway lane in Bowland Forest High, Ribble Valley. Verified against OpenStreetMap on 28 July 2026; no motorcycle-route source was found that names it.

osm-mountain-pass-8c03b5b2e9ec0832.name: Harthope Head (Harthope Moss)
osm-mountain-pass-8c03b5b2e9ec0832.riderNote: At about 627 m the highest public road summit in England, on Harthope Road between St John's Chapel in Weardale and Langdon Beck in Teesdale; Ordnance Survey puts the summit at 630 m. A cattle grid sits on the summit itself. No motorcycle-route source was found that names it.

osm-mountain-pass-953706efc8fa2a93.name: Scarth Nick
osm-mountain-pass-953706efc8fa2a93.riderNote: A 232 m notch through the western edge of the North York Moors on the old drovers' road between Osmotherley and Swainby, mapped three metres wide, with the Sheepwash ford and picnic area immediately below it. No motorcycle-route source was found that names it.
osm-mountain-pass-953706efc8fa2a93.busyPeriods: The Sheepwash picnic area below the nick is a well-used stopping point, so expect parked cars and pedestrians on a three-metre road.

osm-mountain-pass-9c59901e0c5dead8.name: Snake Pass (A57)
osm-mountain-pass-9c59901e0c5dead8.riderNote: The A57 over the Pennines between Glossop and Ladybower, carrying around 30,000 vehicles a week between Manchester and Sheffield. Repeated landslips at Doctor's Gate, Alport, Gillot Hey and Wood Cottage have closed it for extended periods, so check it is open before committing.
osm-mountain-pass-9c59901e0c5dead8.busyPeriods: Commuter-heavy on weekdays and busy with leisure traffic on weekends. Closures and weight limits recur - verify before setting off.
osm-mountain-pass-9c59901e0c5dead8.enforcementNote: The Peak District authority has considered average speed cameras here, and £7.6m of Safer Roads Fund work included motorcyclist-friendly barriers. OSM does not yet record an enforcement relation.

osm-mountain-pass-9f9a6bf868219e7d.name: Cairn o' Mount (B974)
osm-mountain-pass-9f9a6bf868219e7d.riderNote: The B974 Old Military Road over Cairn o' Mount at 454 m, between Fettercairn and Banchory. Simon Weir ranks the Banchory-to-Fettercairn run eighth among Scotland's ten best biking roads, describing mile after quiet mile across the hills.
osm-mountain-pass-9f9a6bf868219e7d.busyPeriods: Snow gates shut this road early and reopen it late - Undiscovered Scotland describes it as often the first road closed by snow and the last to reopen, and Traffic Scotland posts the gate status. Check before committing in winter.

osm-mountain-pass-9ff8ee5e7fcc30dc.name: Barnes Gap (C612)
osm-mountain-pass-9ff8ee5e7fcc30dc.riderNote: A glacial breach carrying the C612 Gorticashel Road through the Sperrins between Gortin and Plumbridge, with the C611 branching at the gap itself. A Northern Ireland motorbike itinerary that names it could not be retrieved, so no motorcycle evidence is recorded.

osm-mountain-pass-ac43e95f49145483.name: Mam Ratagan
osm-mountain-pass-ac43e95f49145483.riderNote: Climbs to around 335 m on the single-track road from Shiel Bridge to Glenelg, with a series of hairpins and a long drop down Glen More to sea level. Often ridden with the Glenelg-Skye ferry and Bealach Udal.
osm-mountain-pass-ac43e95f49145483.busyPeriods: Ferry traffic in season; the ferry runs summer only, so plan the link to Skye around it.

osm-mountain-pass-b323fed09353c81c.name: Kidstones Pass (B6160)
osm-mountain-pass-b323fed09353c81c.riderNote: The B6160 over Kidstones Bank at 425 m, between Bishopdale and Cray at the head of Wharfedale. OpenStreetMap records the south-western climb as 2.9 km and 185 m of ascent, 10% at the start and up to 20% higher up. BestBikingRoads lists the B6160 as a motorcycle road.

osm-mountain-pass-b7d17cb20bc3068f.name: Nick o' Pendle
osm-mountain-pass-b7d17cb20bc3068f.riderNote: The 295 m col carrying the Clitheroe-to-Sabden road over the shoulder of Pendle Hill. Climbfinder measures the Sabden side at 1.3 km averaging 10.9%. Discover Bowland's hill-climb route finishes with a sustained climb here and a fast descent to Clitheroe; the sources found are cycling ones, not motorcycle ones.

osm-mountain-pass-c75db7e461241e4c.name: Cross o' Greet (Lythe Fell Road)
osm-mountain-pass-c75db7e461241e4c.riderNote: The higher of the two fell roads over the eastern Forest of Bowland at 426 m, on the single-track Lythe Fell Road between Slaidburn and High Bentham. Discover Bowland describes a climb up a steep-sided clough and a long, sinuous moorland descent towards Bentham.
osm-mountain-pass-c75db7e461241e4c.busyPeriods: Discover Bowland describes both eastern Bowland fell roads as effectively single track for much of their length across quiet moorland.

osm-mountain-pass-c7cf27a01d29b7b2.name: Kirkstone Pass (A592)
osm-mountain-pass-c7cf27a01d29b7b2.riderNote: At 454 m the highest Lake District pass with a road over it, carrying the A592 from Ambleside to Patterdale and Ullswater. The Ambleside climb is known locally as The Struggle and approaches 1 in 4.
osm-mountain-pass-c7cf27a01d29b7b2.busyPeriods: Busy with Lake District tourist traffic through the summer.

osm-mountain-pass-c88ed185daeb9a44.name: Tullybaccart (A923)
osm-mountain-pass-c88ed185daeb9a44.riderNote: A 213 m crossing of the Sidlaw Hills on the A923 between Coupar Angus and Muirhead, north-west of Dundee. Two lanes, good surface, national speed limit. No motorcycle-route source was found that names it.
osm-mountain-pass-c88ed185daeb9a44.enforcementNote: Police Scotland lists the A923 Coupar Angus to Muirhead as a mobile safety camera route at national speed limit, with sites including Leys and Kettins Junction. OpenStreetMap records no camera or enforcement relation here, so this candidate's derived camera count is zero - a gap in the map, not an absence of enforcement.

osm-mountain-pass-cc76df3713d35fda.name: Wrynose Pass
osm-mountain-pass-cc76df3713d35fda.riderNote: Three miles of narrow, steep pass linking Little Langdale towards the Duddon Valley, almost always ridden as a pair with Hardknott. Sharp hairpins with 1 in 3 and 1 in 4 sections.
osm-mountain-pass-cc76df3713d35fda.busyPeriods: Same as Hardknott - congested on spring and summer weekends.

osm-mountain-pass-d088739b65302cb0.name: Pen-y-Pass (A4086)
osm-mountain-pass-d088739b65302cb0.riderNote: The 359 m summit of the Llanberis Pass, where the A4086 runs between the Glyderau and the Snowdon massif from Capel Curig to Llanberis. Two lanes at the national limit, and the busiest mountain road in Eryri.
osm-mountain-pass-d088739b65302cb0.busyPeriods: The Pen-y-Pass car park is often full before 8am on weekends and busy summer days, and busy weekends are booked out weeks ahead - expect queueing and drivers hunting for parking on the pass itself from early morning through the season.

osm-mountain-pass-d151fc22c5e1ce67.name: Waddington Fell (B6478)
osm-mountain-pass-d151fc22c5e1ce67.riderNote: The B6478 Slaidburn Road over Waddington Fell at 355 m, the main Clitheroe-to-Slaidburn route and the least remote of the Bowland crossings. Verified against OpenStreetMap on 28 July 2026; no motorcycle-route source was found that names it.

osm-mountain-pass-d71d38d41218d2d0.name: Top o' Dent
osm-mountain-pass-d71d38d41218d2d0.riderNote: A 421 m saddle on a single-track unclassified lane above Dent, Westmorland and Furness. Verified against OpenStreetMap on 28 July 2026; no motorcycle-route source was found that names it.

osm-mountain-pass-d813357d9d494042.name: Bealach Udal
osm-mountain-pass-d813357d9d494042.riderNote: The steep pass on the Kylerhea road on Skye, reached from the Glenelg ferry. Ranked the fifth hardest climb in Scotland by Simon Warren, it is narrow with passing places rather than a two-lane pass.
osm-mountain-pass-d813357d9d494042.busyPeriods: Tied to the seasonal Glenelg ferry; otherwise lightly used.

osm-mountain-pass-e86bd88912b12d5f.name: Hardknott Pass
osm-mountain-pass-e86bd88912b12d5f.riderNote: Shares the title of steepest road in Britain at 1 in 3, with 33% gradients on several hairpins and an undulating surface. Barely one car wide in places, connecting Eskdale with the Duddon Valley.
osm-mountain-pass-e86bd88912b12d5f.busyPeriods: Avoid summer weekends - much of it is single track and it jams with cars and cyclists. A weekday is a different road.

osm-mountain-pass-f0a2a2097066d2d9.name: Killhope Cross (A689)
osm-mountain-pass-f0a2a2097066d2d9.riderNote: At 627 m the highest point on any A road in England, where the A689 crosses the Durham/Cumbria watershed between Cowshill and Nenthead. Ordnance Survey names it Britain's highest-elevation major road. No motorcycle-route source was found that names it.

node/732132339.reason: Glasnakille Road, a dead-end single-track lane on Skye at 100 m. Not a pass, and it leads nowhere a group ride would route through.

node/2308216337.reason: An unnamed saddle at 242 m on the A4113 near the Shropshire/Herefordshire border. A good A-road hill crossing, but not a mountain pass, and the A4113 is already a road-layer candidate on its own way geometry.
node/2308216337.roadLayerCoverage: A4113 is already published in the road layer.

node/2308216342.reason: An unnamed unclassified lane near Shelderton at 278 m, with only tracks and footways around it. Too minor to offer as a destination road.

node/280187024.reason: An unnamed saddle at 261 m on the A928 in Angus, north of Dundee. A reasonable moorland-edge road, not a pass. No road-layer candidate covers the A928, so this crossing is not offered at all - a road-layer scoring question, not a reason to publish it as a pass.
node/280187024.roadLayerCoverage: No A928 candidate in the road layer.

node/271799539.reason: An unnamed node on the A859, the spine road of Harris, where the B897 branches off. The road is well worth riding and is already a road-layer candidate; this point is not a named pass.
node/271799539.roadLayerCoverage: A859 is already published in the road layer.

node/8500938038.reason: An unnamed node on the B9120 over the Hill of Garvock, Aberdeenshire, an asphalt secondary road at the national limit. A pleasant secondary road, already a road-layer candidate; the summit is not a pass.
node/8500938038.roadLayerCoverage: B9120 is already published in the road layer.

node/33624619.reason: An unnamed node at 152 m on the A3055 Bonchurch Road on the Isle of Wight. Offering this as a mountain pass would discredit the whole layer.

node/3906229915.reason: An unnamed node at 147 m on the B954 near Hatton, Angus. An ordinary rural junction area with no pass character.
